subject: Post-demo: ProbeLabs competitive economics & validation runbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@probelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: ProbeLabs competitive economics & validation runbook

Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Objective recap: ProbeLabs wants a predictable production inference stack for their conversational agents with a target P95 latency <= 220ms and a blended cost target near $10 / 1M tokens for steady-state traffic. Primary constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data, multi-region read replicas, and a strict procurement window in Q1.

- What we heard from your team: 60% of calls are short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64–512), 10% long tails; they expect bursty e-commerce traffic (x3 day-of-sale spikes).

- Competitive positioning notes we discussed (high level):
  * Hyperscaler A (managed endpoints): easy ops but higher baseline per-token when unbatched; effective for short-tail bursts if you pay for overprovisioned capacity.
  * Hyperscaler B (VM-managed GPUs): lower raw GPU unit cost but higher orchestration and cold-start penalties unless you maintain warm pools.
  * Other inference APIs: some offer attractive headline throughput, but lack prefix/KV caching and fine-grained quantization profiles that reduce token burn on repeated contexts.

- Redwood differentiators (callouts we should validate in POC):
  1) Automatic prefix/KV caching — improves effective token economics on repeated context (search + recall)
  2) Model-variant routing and graceful fallback — keeps SLAs during capacity storms
  3) Quantization profiles tuned per-workload — meaningful CPU/GPU savings for medium+ sequence lengths

Proposed immediate next steps (short, executable):
1) ProbeLabs to send a 7-day anonymized token histogram + a sample of 50 representative requests (we can accept redacted text) — Alex/Priya to share by EOD Monday.
2) Redwood to run a small-proof runbook (non-prod) with three configurations and return per-1M-token and P95 latency numbers:
   A) Redwood hosted default (no quant) — baseline throughput/cost
   B) Redwood + batching (dynamic, up to 128) + prefix cache enabled — measure cache-hit sensitivity at 30/50/70%
   C) Redwood + int8 quant profile + batching — aggressive econ path
   Deliverable: CSV with tokens consumed, compute seconds, estimated $/1M tokens. ETA: run complete in 5 business days after we get the histogram.
3) Internal sync: Ben & Karthik to prepare a short packet that maps the above runs to a recommended production configuration and a conservative TCO estimate for Q1 procurement.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short runbook and a template CSV for the histogram (validation-runbook.md, probelabs-raw-costs.csv).

If that aligns, Alex — confirm timeline for the histogram and sample requests and we’ll schedule the validation window.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: validation-runbook.md)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@probelabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya.s@probelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ProbeLabs competitive economics & validation runbook

Marissa — thanks for the succinct recap. We’ll start pulling the histogram and the 50-sample set; Priya will lead on this. Quick clarifications before we run the export: 

- The traffic histogram will be tokenized using our in-house tokenizer (same as the models you tested). Should be fine; we’ll include a mapping note.
- For sensitive fields we will replace PHI with stable tokens (REDACTED_1, etc.). Is that acceptable for your cache-hit tests?

Two quick asks from our side to make the comparison meaningful: 
1) Can Redwood include an unbatched baseline number and an explicitly documented RPC overhead per request? Hyperscaler vendors are quoting per-request overheads that materially affect cost for short requests.
2) In the run CSV, please include a column for "tokens_billed" vs "tokens_sent" so we can see how caching/prefix optimization changes billing semantics.

We can get the exports to you by Tuesday EOD PST. Also attaching our raw per-hour GPU utilization logs for last month (probelabs-raw-costs.csv) — we expect that will help your sizing.

If all good, I’ll block the validation window for next Thursday and Friday.

— Alex
Head of ML Platform, ProbeLabs
(attachment: probelabs-raw-costs.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: quick competitive checks before validation

Couple of operational guardrails to add to the runbook: 

- Ensure we measure at 3 cache-hit rates: native (as-is), simulated 50%, and simulated 70% — ProbeLabs’ pattern (60% short, repeated contexts) suggests caching will be the dominant factor.
- For unbatched baselines, include the 95th percentile RPC overhead (ns/CPU) and a per-request inflight memory footprint. Hyperscaler A’s published docs hide some of these numbers behind different billing assumptions (e.g., billed per-chunk vs per-token).
- Capture cold-start impact: run a fresh node restart and measure the first 200 requests to surface KV warmup costs. This will be useful for their bursty spike profile.

Also: preliminary econ math from demo notes — rough back-of-envelope:
  * Hyperscaler managed: ~$28 / 1M tokens (unbatched, no cache)
  * Redwood hosted baseline: ~$12 / 1M tokens (unbatched)
  * Redwood with 70% cache-hit & batching to 128: effective $3.2 / 1M tokens (dominant savings from cache + reduced compute)

I’ll capture the formulas so the final CSV includes columns: raw_compute_seconds, gpu_cost_usd, batching_factor, cache_hit_rate, effective_usd_per_1M.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Eng — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@probelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ProbeLabs competitive economics & validation runbook

Alex / Priya — great, thanks for the quick turnaround commitment. Two small updates before we start: 

1) On PHI/redaction: redacted tokens are fine — we’ll use stable placeholders to preserve cache and repetition behavior. Please include a short mapping doc in the Drive folder.
2) We will publish both "tokens_sent" and "tokens_billed" columns and a short README documenting how Redwood defines billed tokens vs what we measure (billed excludes cached prefix tokens when cache hits are observed in our infra).

Validation schedule we agreed:
- Tuesday (you deliver histogram + samples + util logs) — we ingest and sanity-check.
- Thursday/Friday next week — Redwood runs three configs across a small fixture (non-prod) and returns a CSV + short slide with recommended prod config.

Ben / Karthik: please attach the run command snippets and the cost-mapping sheet to the Drive folder after this message. Alex — I’ll create the HubSpot activity and the Drive folder now and share links.

Thanks all — looking forward to a tight, numbers-first validation.

Cheers,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-proposal-1M-token-breakdown.pdf)
